title: V for Vendetta to return to theaters for 20th anniversary — Rolling Stone - UA.NEWS
content:
The 2006 film V for Vendetta will return to the big screen for its 20th anniversary. Screenings will take place only on November 1 and 5. The anniversary re-release is being organized by Fathom Entertainment, Warner Bros. and DC Vertigo, Rolling Stone reports. A new trailer was released for the anniversary, featuring a reimagined version of Tchaikovsky’s 1812 Overture. It was created by Jonathan Snipes of the hip-hop group Clipping. The screenings will also be accompanied by a new special video feature with director James McTeigue. In it, he discusses the mythology of V’s character and why the ideas of freedom and resistance raised in the film still resonate. More current news is available on the UA.News Telegram channel Telegram. V for Vendetta is based on the graphic novel by Alan Moore and David Lloyd. The film tells the story of the masked V, played by Hugo Weaving, and his struggle against totalitarian Britain, where immigrants, members of the LGBTQ+ community and political dissidents are forced into silence and later disappear. After V saves Evey, played by Natalie Portman, she learns about his tragic past and discovers the truth about herself. She later joins the revolution against the fascist government. The film also stars Stephen Rea, Stephen Fry, John Hurt, Roger Allam, Tim Pigott-Smith and Rupert Graves. The Wachowskis served as the film’s producers. title: ‘V for Vendetta’ Returns to Theaters After 20 Years - Rolling Stone
content: Twenty years after theaters debuted V for Vendetta, the film is set to return to the big screen. The classic will run for two nights only, on Nov. 1 and Nov. 5, for the anniversary event, courtesy of Fathom Entertainment, Warner Bros., and DC Vertigo. The showings will also be accompanied by a new featurette with director James McTeigue, who reflects on the enduring mythology of V and why the film’s ideas of freedom and resistance still resonate today. To mark the occasion, an anniversary trailer was released on Friday and includes a reimagining of Tchaikovsky’s 1812 Overture by Jonathan Snipes of the hip-hop group Clipping. Based on the graphic novel by Alan Moore and David Lloyd, V for Vendetta tells the story of the masked “V” (Hugo Weaving) and his fight against a totalitarian Britain where immigrants, the LGBTQ community, and political dissidents are silenced and disappear. In the clip, after he rescues a working class woman named Evey (Natalie Portman), she learns about his devastating past and uncovers the truth about herself — achieved through some questionable imprisonment — joining the revolution against the fascist government. Alongside stunning performances by Portman and Weaving, the Wachowskis-produced film also features memorable portrayals by Stephen Rea, Stephen Fry, John Hurt, Roger Allam, Tim Pigott-Smith, and Rupert Graves. “The award-winning V for Vendetta graphic novel led to one of the most provocative films in the early 2000s. Twenty years later, V for Vendetta still asks the questions that matter: about freedom, identity, and who gets to speak up,” Shannah Miller, Vice President of Marketing at Fathom Entertainment, said in a statement. “Fathom is thrilled to bring this great movie back to theatres, featuring an exclusive new conversation with director James McTeigue for a whole new generation of audiences.” Tickets for the 20th anniversary of V for Vendetta are available online and at participating theaters. title: The Next Chevrolet Trax Will Put Another Nail In Honda HR-V's Coffin - CarBuzz
content: Subscribe to the CarBuzz newsletter to never miss an update Once upon a time, the Chevrolet Trax was something of a joke. Then a few years ago, Chevy saw fit to redesign the small crossover inside and out. To say it was a hit is an understatement – Trax is the best-selling subcompact SUV in America, and if these new spy shots are any indication, it will probably stay that way. If we were on the Honda HR-V design team, we'd be working overtime to find some new ideas. This Chevy is looking untouchable As previously mentioned, the current Trax is a few years old so a mid-cycle refresh is due. We haven't seen much in the way of prototypes out and about, but this particular sighting makes up for it by showing us pretty much everything. In fact, there's not a stitch of camouflage anywhere to be seen. And what do we see? This refresh won't be some new headlights and a new shade of gray. The front fascia is new, sticking with the open-mouth look but stretching a little further to the sides. The grille doesn't dip as far down, leaving room for a slightly larger lower grille in the center. There are new headlights, but they aren't reshaped housings in the same location. The current Trax stashes its headlights in vertical housings on the sides of the fascia, but the facelift moves them inward a bit. The entire vertical light cluster is gone now, but the small SUV will keep its split-light arrangement with thin running lights at the top. The result is a cleaner, more proportioned look. It's a good look. There are noteworthy changes at the rear, too. Actually this update is rather clever. At a glance, it appears designers gave the refreshed Trax completely new taillights in new quarter panels. Instead of chunky housings on the corners, new lenses are slimmer and extend across the hatch, connecting with thin black trim in the middle. It's a modern look that aligns with industry trends. But look closely. The new taillights on the corners look like they occupy the same space as the current ones. The main housings taper inward, but that gap is taken up by the new rear fascia. If you put new quarter panels next to old ones, we bet a gazillion dollars they line up. And since we're already looking at the rear fascia, the new design removes large red reflectors in the corners for smaller, slimmer ones. And it appears the new fascia fits with the existing hatch, which now gets cutouts for the taillights and black trim stretching across it. So really, while the rear looks quite a bit different, the only items actually changing are the fascia and lights. Sadly, we don't get a glimpse inside, but previous reports suggest some notable changes are taking place for the dash. A slightly larger touchscreen with a cleaner, tidier look to mirror the outside is a safe bet. Chevy designers are at boss-level when it comes to making an aging design look fresh while sticking to a budget. Some new lights and fascias give the already attractive Trax a sharp, modern makeover, and those parts aren't that expensive to create. And Chevrolet would be wise to stick as close to the budget as possible. Amid record-high fuel prices and average new-vehicle costs over $50,000, the current Trax is one of America's least expensive new vehicles with a starting price under $24,000, destination included. No wonder the company sold over 200,000 last year, beating the Subaru Crosstrek and demolishing the Honda HR-V. But keeping that price in check is vital to Trax maintaining its status as lord of subcompact SUVs. Considering this prototype was caught without any camo, expect a full reveal coming very soon. title: Final Trailer for 'V for Vendetta' 20th Anniversary Re-Release in Nov - FirstShowing
content: by Alex Billington September 18, 2026Source: YouTube "By the power of truth, I, while living, have conquered the universe." 💥 "Vi veri universum vivus vici." Fathom Ent. has revealed one final "get your tickets" trailer for the special screenings of the extraordinary revolutionary classic V for Vendetta, made by The Wachowskis and director James McTeigue. The 2026 event will be held on November 5th, 2026 in celebration of the 20th Anniversary of the movie (it was originally released back in March 2006 but the date November 5th is important in the movie). With another viewing on November 1st as well. V for Vendetta is one of my all-time favorites, a brilliantly exhilarating cinematic experience, and one of The Wachowski Sisters' most unforgettable follow-ups to The Matrix just 7 years prior. In a near future British dystopian authoritarian society (similar to the one in America today), a shadowy freedom fighter, known only by the alias of "V", plots to overthrow the tyrannical government with the help of a young woman. Natalie Portman stars as Evey, and Hugo Weaving co-stars entirely under a Guy Fawkes mask in one his best performances ever as the enigmatic V. The cast includes Stephen Rea, Stephen Fry, John Hurt, Tim Pigott-Smith, Rupert Graves, & Roger Allam. November 5th is right around the corner and let me say – this is the movie we all need at this moment in time. As powerful as ever. Here's the final 20th Anniversary promo trailer for James McTeigue's V for Vendetta, from YouTube: You can view the 2025 trailer for Fathom's V for Vendetta 20th Anniv. screenings right here from last year. In the near future, Evey Hammond (Natalie Portman) is an average citizen in the UK, which is under the rule of the fascist & tyrannical Norsefire Party. She is an employee of the state-run British TV Network, but soon, she becomes the number one enemy of the state with an enigmatic & larger-than-life freedom fighter known only by the letter "V" (Hugo Weaving). V informs Evey she must hide in his underground lair for at least one year, and while she is reluctant to the idea at first, a bond soon forms between them. In the meantime, the mysterious past of V is gradually revealed to the police inspector tasked with finding him, Eric Finch, and it is not long until he starts questioning everything that his government stands for... V for Vendetta is directed by Australian filmmaker James McTeigue, directing his very first big movie at the time before going on to make Ninja Assassin (2009), The Raven (2012), and Survivor (2015) after. The screenplay is written by The Wachowski Sisters - Lilly & Lana Wachowski. Adapted from the famous graphic novel written by Alan Moore (who removed his name from the credits) and illustrated by David Lloyd, first published in 1982. Produced by The Wachowskis, Joel Silver, and Grant Hill. Warner Bros first released V for Vendetta in theaters starting March 17th, 2026 - earning a total of $70M at the US box office that year. The extra point cut Elmira's lead to 21-7. Geneva leads Waterloo 20-0 after the first quarter in Seneca Falls. Tyler Reger intercepted Victor quarterback Eli Ricci, then caught a touchdown pass from Matt Kosiorek to extend Hilton's lead to 21-0 with 8:08 remaining in the second quarter. It was Kosiorek's third touchdown pass of the first half and Reger's second touchdown reception. Matt Kosiorek connected with Jared Wade for his second long touchdown pass of the first quarter, extending Hilton's lead over Victor to 14-0 with 1:09 remaining. Brendan Mangone connected with Imani Wagstaff for a 14-yard touchdown pass to give Rush-Henrietta a 14-6 lead with 7:08 remaining in the second quarter. Fast-moving first quarter ends without points. The Cadets scored quickly after forcing Victor to punt on its opening possession. James Mobley Jr. scored on a 4-yard run, and East/World of Inquiry added the extra point to take a 7-6 lead over Monroe with 1:40 remaining in the second quarter. Aquinas (0-2) is looking for its first win of the season. Terrell “Pooty” Cunningham Jr. connected with James Brumfield II for his 77th career touchdown pass, setting the Section V record. Brumfield made the catch on a perfectly placed pass to give Monroe a 6-0 lead late in the first quarter. title: Brentford vs Chelsea player ratings: Henderson a vocal leader as Thiago lifts weight off shoulders - BBC
content: Brentford stay unbeaten as they put three past Chelsea Brentford climbed to third in the Premier League with an impressive 3-0 victory over Chelsea. Goals from Jaidon Anthony, Igor Thiago and substitute Fabio Carvalho secured the three points as Chelsea's winless league run extended to three matches. Here's how I rated the players and you can see how you scored them below. Caoimhin Kelleher: An accomplished display, although he was never required to make any outstanding saves. 6 Michael Kayode: Played a couple of sloppy passes and rarely ventured forward. 6 Kristoffer Ajer: A sizeable presence at the back despite coming under significant pressure from crosses in open play and from set-pieces. 7 Jannik Schuster: The young defender excelled in his own box but looked nervous in possession on a few occasions, including an overhit backpass that could have led to an own goal. He then set up the winner. 7 Keane Lewis-Potter: A poor clearance led to a Neto chance in the 10th minute, but he was impressive on the counter-attack. That perhaps owed something to his experience of learning the left-back role after previously playing as an attacker. 6 Yehor Yarmoliuk: On his 100th appearance, he threatened with a powerful long-range effort in the 37th minute and created Brentford's best chance shortly after half-time. 7 Vitaly Janelt: Did just enough to halt a Cole Palmer dribble early on, although he risked conceding a penalty. He provided a physical presence in midfield, with a potential Germany debut on the horizon under new manager Jurgen Klopp. 7 Mikkel Damsgaard: The Dane was not at his usual level from set-pieces or with his shooting from distance until he delivered an incredible whipped corner that led to the opening goal. 6 Kevin Schade: The in-form forward produced several pressure-relieving dribbles and had a shot blocked in the first half. Played a part in the final two goals. 7 Igor Thiago: The Brazil international was on a four-game goalless run before kick-off and worked hard but struggled in front of goal. He eventually delivered with a late strike to seal victory and his celebration looked like a weight then lifted off his shoulders, along with his Brentford shirt. 7 Jaidon Anthony: After a quiet first half, he missed his side's best chance early in the second half but responded well to score the opener. 7 Mamadou Sangare (on 72, Yarmoliuk): Did his combative duties well. 7 Fabio Carvalho (on 87, Damsgaard): Ghosted in nicely to add a goal late on in a very short spell on the pitch. 7 Emiliano Martinez: The Argentine did not face any clear chances or difficult set-pieces in the first half. There was little he could do about Brentford's opener. 6 Wesley Fofana: The Frenchman was a physical presence at the back and dealt well enough with Brentford's long balls but was taken off for Josh Acheampong in the 72nd minute. 6 Maxence Lacroix: He coped well with Igor Thiago for most of the match, winning the majority of his duels, but he gave the ball away for Brentford's second goal and he missed a clear chance in the dying moments. 4 Levi Colwill: A quiet match by his high standards after being left out of the England squad. 6 Pedro Neto: His well-struck effort was saved in the 10th minute. He was lively throughout, linking up well in attack and stretching Brentford with his pace. 6 Jordan Henderson: There were no signs of rust. After receiving some early boos, he settled into the game and looked a vocal leader on the pitch. He also put some good corners into the box. 7 Valentin Barco: On his first Premier League start, the Argentine impressed defensively and was more ambitious with his passing than Henderson. 6 Pep Chavarria: Produced some dangerous crosses and was tidy in possession. A largely positive display despite one piece of naive defending in the first half that led to a free-kick. 7 Cole Palmer: Undoubtedly Chelsea's best player on the night, with much of their attacking play going through him. However, he was unable to produce the decisive moment he craved, with a free-kick comfortably saved and few other clear opportunities. He also worked hard defensively. 7 Danny Welbeck: On his first Premier League start for Chelsea, the 35-year-old created a chance for Neto but did not do enough to compensate for the absence of injured striker Joao Pedro. His 72nd minute withdrawal said a lot. 5 Morgan Rogers: Had a dangerous effort blocked in the penalty area just before half-time. The club-record £117m signing could also have done more to win the header at the back post for Brentford's opener. He ended the match playing up front as a striker. 5 Josh Acheampong (on 72, Fofana): It was unclear why Acheampong came on when he did and, as a young defender, didn't make much impact in these circumstances. 6 Geovany Quenda (on 72, Welbeck): Impressively got on the ball often and tried to make something happen for Chelsea but without any results. 6 Subs not used: Penders, Gusto, Hato, Lavia, Gittens After the opportunity to rate players has closed, the score displayed represents the average from all the submissions by BBC Sport users. title: Booking Holdings v European Commission: EU General Court Confirms Theories of Harm Can Travel Across an Ecosystem - JD Supra
content:
On 9 September 2026, the European Union’s General Court delivered its judgment in Booking Holdings v European Commission (Case T-1139/23), confirming the European Commission’s (Commission’s) decision in Booking Holdings/eTraveli (M.10615) to prohibit Booking’s acquisition of eTraveli. This is the first merger blocked on the basis of a pure ecosystem theory of harm. The judgment, which may still be appealed to the EU’s top court, reinforces the Commission’s ability to challenge mergers involving ecosystem tie-ups by allegedly dominant players. In November 2021, Booking, the largest hotel online travel agency (OTA) in the European Economic Area (EEA), agreed to acquire eTraveli, a leading flight OTA. Although the transaction did not meet the EU merger thresholds, it was referred to the Commission at the parties’ request. In September 2023, the Commission blocked the merger.1 Its prohibition rested on the theory that the acquisition would strengthen Booking’s already dominant position in the hotel OTA market by enabling it to develop a “travel ecosystem” and increase opportunities for cross-selling accommodations. By acquiring eTraveli, the Commission found that Booking would attract a significant number of additional customers earlier in their travel-booking journeys. The case was the first in which the Commission based merger objections on a novel “reverse leveraging” theory of harm. The Commission acknowledged that the theory was not squarely addressed in the Non-Horizontal Merger Guidelines (Guidelines), noting that: Booking would leverage its ability to acquire customers in the neighbouring flight OTA market to strengthen its dominant position in the hotel OTA market. […], such circumstances, referred to by the Notifying Party as ‘reverse leveraging’2, were not explicitly foreseen in the Non-Horizontal Guidelines but nor were they excluded from them. Such circumstances, […], have risen only more recently with the development of online ecosystems. The Commission said its argument was in line with its 2019 report “Competition Policy for the Digital Era” and indicated that for a company operating in an ecosystem which benefits from strong positive network effects, “the risk […] extends to the strengthening of dominance as it fortifies the dominance of the ecosystem.” In April 2026, the Commission published the Draft Merger Guidelines (DMG) indicating, based on its assessment of Booking Holdings/eTraveli, that a merger may result in a significant impediment to effective competition “when it leads to the entrenchment of a dominant position […] across closely related markets, which may consist of one or several distinct but interconnected markets (‘ecosystem’).” The DMG also note that the Commission may assess merging firms’ existing market power by taking into account “how relevant the ecosystem is for effectively competing in the core market.” The Commission rejected Booking’s efficiency claims, including those based on the elimination of double marginalization, which the DMG recognize as a valid merger synergy. The Commission’s skepticism in this case was partly based on the lack of anticipated consumer benefits in Booking’s internal documents. Booking proposed commitments that included a choice screen on the flight checkout page and displaying hotel offers from competing OTAs on Booking.com and eTraveli brand platforms. The Commission rejected these behavioral commitments, among other reasons, because it said they did not remove Booking’s cross-selling opportunities across hotel services to flight customers and were difficult to monitor. The judgment concluded that the Commission’s assessment did not contradict the Guidelines. The General Court found that the Guidelines reserved for the Commission a right to apply and further develop theories of harm not expressly set out in the text. This is particularly relevant in digital markets, as their specific characteristics were not yet known — and therefore not sufficiently taken into account — when the Guidelines were published in 2008. On that basis, the General Court determined that the Commission’s approach, including the focus on “reverse leveraging,” was permissible. The General Court also pointed out that the Commission may, where appropriate, account for credible and realistic future market developments in constructing the counterfactual scenario. The General Court was not wholly in agreement with the Commission’s approach, however, taking a critical stance towards certain elements of the Commission’s analysis, which the General Court found was “vitiated by a number of errors.” The General Court determined that: Ultimately, despite its criticisms, the General Court excused these errors, noting that the Commission may base its assessments on qualitative elements, provided that the “evidence [...] is sufficiently cogent and consistent.” The General Court emphasized that the substantial market gap between Booking and its competitors, combined with strong network effects and the fact that the increment would be achieved in a channel which Booking does not yet dominate, would create a travel ecosystem difficult for competitors to replicate. The judgment thus affirmed a finding of anticompetitive foreclosure effects sufficient to prohibit a merger despite the very limited share increment in the dominated market post-transaction, and on the basis that the merger would make the dominant position less contestable and consolidate a low level of competition. This is a fairly low evidentiary standard, which the Commission may interpret as latitude to challenge acquisitions by dominant companies beyond what is contemplated in the DMG. The General Court also upheld the Commission’s rejection of Booking’s claimed efficiencies. Several efficiency arguments were found inadmissible on account of procedural errors. On substance, the General Court shared the Commission’s skepticism regarding the marginal cost reduction claim because Booking’s internal documents did not show that the claimed benefits would be passed on to consumers. The General Court also rejected out-of-market efficiencies in the form of price reduction in the flight OTA market, noting that only those efficiencies which relate to the markets susceptible to competitive harm (in this case, the hotel OTA) and which are capable of counterbalancing the anticompetitive effects are relevant to the analysis. The General Court found limited commonality between the two consumer groups. Although the DMG allow for out-of-market efficiencies to alleviate competition concerns, the DMG also presuppose that the harmed and benefiting consumers are “substantially the same.” The Booking ruling, which may still be appealed to the EU’s top court, confirms the increasing relevance of ecosystems in merger control assessment and now lends judicial support to the entrenchment theory of harm introduced in the DMG. It remains to be seen whether this theory of harm will gain importance in the context of the EU Digital Markets Act and the gatekeepers’ obligation to report deals, and whether the judgment may prompt large companies to engage in cooperation agreements with service providers in adjacent markets, in lieu of acquisitions. The ruling also accepts the Commission’s expansive interpretation of its own Guidelines, here based on the characteristics of digital markets, which were not fully reflected in the 2008 Guidelines. Amid increasing consideration of efficiencies, companies should consider documenting pro-competitive aspects of their contemplated transactions early and ensure that those are verifiable, merger-specific and benefit consumers. The DMG recognize that mergers combining complementary products or technologies may reduce transaction costs and increase interoperability, which could help counter an ecosystem theory of harm. Knowledge strategy legal specialist Rayhane Ricci contributed to this article. 1 In contrast, the UK Competition and Markets Authority (CMA) cleared the transaction in Phase 1, finding limited evidence that a flight OTA offering is, or could become, a particularly significant customer retention and acquisition channel for hotel OTA services. 2 The reverse leveraging effect was described by the General Court in the judgment as “the merged entity [using] its position on a market in which it does not have market power (the flight OTA market) to strengthen its allegedly dominant position on another market (the hotel OTA market).” By contrast, traditional leveraging consists of using dominance in one market to extend market power to another (nondominant) market. title: Nottingham Forest v Coventry City: Key stats and talking points - Yahoo Sports
content: Nottingham Forest earned their first win of the season last weekend and now face a bottom-of-the-table Coventry City side yet to score or avoid defeat since their return to the Premier League. It's the first top-flight meeting between the clubs since a 4-0 home win for the Sky Blues in January 1999. Nottingham Forest answered Oliver Glasner's call to find the "final bit missing" when they deservedly beat Aston Villa last weekend. Head coach Glasner was referring to his team's goalscoring issues but it could just as easily apply to their troublesome home form. So far this season at the City Ground, Forest have lost twice to Leeds United – including in the Carabao Cup – and drawn with Spurs. They failed to score in any of those games and seldom threatened to do so, registering a combined seven shots on target. It's the continuation of an issue which dates back to last year; their only home league victory in 13 attempts since Christmas came against soon-to-be-relegated Burnley in April. Only Tottenham have earned fewer points at home among Premier League ever-present sides during that time, while Forest are the lowest scorers in front of their own fans. The momentum of a Championship title-winning campaign has swiftly dissipated for Coventry, who are yet to earn a point since returning to the Premier League and made a midweek exit from the EFL Cup. After 97 league goals last season, they have none after four top-flight games; Mustapha Hadji remains the last Coventry player to score a Premier League goal, on 5 May 2001. This is the first time since their debut 1919-20 campaign that Coventry have lost their opening four league fixtures in a season, while they are only the fifth side in English top-flight history to do so without scoring. The Sky Blues are creating chances, though, and have an expected goals tally of 4.2. Perhaps not enough of those opportunities are falling to the right players. Coventry have had 41 attempts on goal in the Premier League but only nine were by centre-forwards, rising to 23 – a modest 56% – when incorporating all attacking players. Surprisingly, six clubs have a lower percentage but only Coventry have a defender with his side's most goal attempts – Bobby Thomas, with nine. Despite Coventry's current travails, history offers them hope: eight of the previous 18 teams to start a Premier League season with four straight defeats managed to stay up. And Frank Lampard's side can take inspiration from the fact Crystal Palace lost their opening seven games without scoring in 2017-18 but rallied to finish 11th.

title: Currents - Energy Industry Insights, V 10, Issue 9, 2026 - JD Supra
content:
Welcome to our ninth issue of Currents – our energy industry insights e-newsletter – for 2026. Derrick Price Williamson
Senior Editor, Currents
Member in Charge of Harrisburg Office Barry A. Naum
Chief Content Editor, Currents
Member, Co-Chair of Utility Law Group Jamie L. Martines
Assistant Editor, Currents
Associate By Luke Sternick, Spilman Thomas & Battle Law Clerk Following the capture of Venezuelan leader Nicolás Maduro, the U.S. secured a 100-year concession in Venezuela’s oil fields. As reported by The New York Times, tensions between the U.S. and Venezuela rose significantly in the years leading up to Maduro’s arrest. During Trump’s first term, the Justice Department indicted Maduro in March 2020 with Narco-Terrorism, Corruption, Drug Trafficking and Other Criminal Charges. The Biden administration recognized Venezuela’s opposition leader, Edmundo González, following Venezuela’s disputed 2024 presidential election. In 2025, Trump designated Maduro as the leader of the Cartel de los Soles and described the organization as a Venezuela-based criminal group. Throughout the fall of 2025, Trump ordered controversial strikes on Venezuelan boats and killed 11 “terrorists” allegedly transporting drugs to the United States. On December 16, 2025, Trump ordered a blockade of sanctioned oil tankers in Venezuela. The tension between the U.S. and Venezuela culminated in the extraction of Venezuela’s acting president during Operation Absolute Resolve. “The rule change, first proposed last year, represents a fundamental shift from efforts by Democratic Presidents Joe Biden and Barack Obama to address climate change and regulate carbon dioxide and other greenhouse gases that trap the sun’s heat.” Why this is important: On September 14, 2026, the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) announced that it is repealing limits on greenhouse gas emissions emitted by the nation's fossil fuel-fired power plants. According to the EPA, the repeal of these limits will save the energy industry more than $300 billion in costs and will promote American energy. In addition to the repeal, the EPA announced that it is planning to prevent future administrations from regulating climate pollution from power plants. Environmental groups are expected to legally challenge both the repeal and the effort to limit future administrations from regulating greenhouse gas emissions from power plants. While the outcome of any forthcoming legal challenge is unknown, if the repeal is maintained, then power plant owners, including utilities, will have greater flexibility to maintain and extend the lives of existing fossil fuel plants or even build new plants. --- Steven W. Lee West Virginia Sues Pennsylvania Over Energy Credit Limits “West Virginia argues that Pennsylvania violates the Commerce Clause by favoring its power producers over businesses from other states.” Why this is important: A lawsuit filed in federal court by West Virginia Attorney General JB McCuskey and naming the Pennsylvania Utility Commission (PUC), PUC Chairman Stephen DeFrank, and Vice Chair Kimberley Barrow is challenging the constitutionality of laws restricting the sale of energy credits by out-of-state companies to Pennsylvania power companies. The lawsuit argues that Pennsylvania violates the Commerce Clause by favoring Pennsylvania energy producers over those from other states. It seeks to open up competition for energy credit sales in Pennsylvania to power producers across the PJM Interconnection power grid footprint. Under Pennsylvania’s Alternative Energy Portfolio Standards Act (AEPS) of 2004 and subsequent amendments, power companies must obtain 18 percent of the power they sell from certain approved sources. One way they can meet that standard is through buying energy credits sold by power producers. Initially, energy producers from across the PJM Interconnection power grid footprint could sell credits in Pennsylvania. But state laws passed in recent years limit sales of energy credits to Pennsylvania companies only. This prevents West Virginia companies from selling energy credits to Pennsylvania power companies. The lawsuit argues that, as a result of these policies, West Virginia power producers missed out on more than $25 million in energy credit sales in 2025. Those sales could have been used to offset power bills for West Virginia customers, the lawsuit states. --- Jamie L. Martines US Electric Co-Ops Call EPA Gas Plant Rule 'Untenable' as Data Center Demand Surges “The executives claim it has been harder to keep up with rising electricity demand from data centers and other large users — but a repeal would mean more planet-warming pollution for communities already bearing the costs of a hotter, less stable climate, as Utility Dive reported.” Why this is important: The nation’s electric cooperatives are calling for changes to federal energy policy as utilities face growing electricity demand and concerns about grid reliability and affordability. The National Rural Electric Cooperative Association (NRECA), which represents nearly 900 electric cooperatives serving approximately 42 million Americans, has urged federal policymakers to address constraints on electricity generation and transmission while maintaining reliable and affordable power. The issue is particularly significant for rural utilities, which often face substantial infrastructure and transmission challenges while serving geographically dispersed customers. NRECA has recently pressed the Environmental Protection Agency to fully repeal the 2024 power-plant greenhouse-gas rule, arguing that regulatory requirements could affect the availability and cost of electricity. The developments could create opportunities for utilities and energy companies navigating federal environmental requirements, generation projects, transmission infrastructure, and related regulatory proceedings. --- Jason Wandling Interior Releases Major Update on Coal Potential Beneath Federal Lands “356 billion short tons in the lower 48, led by Wyoming, and at least 140 billion short tons in Alaska – enough to last 600 years.” Why this is important: The U.S. Department of the Interior released a U.S. Geological Survey assessment identifying substantial coal resources beneath federally managed lands, potentially creating new opportunities for coal development and federal leasing. The assessment estimates 4.2 billion short tons of reported coal reserves associated with active mines and an additional 356 billion short tons of available coal resources in the lower 48 states. At current U.S. consumption rates, those resources could supply the nation’s coal needs for at least 600 years. The assessment may have significant implications for companies considering federal coal leases, particularly as Interior evaluates how to manage and develop these resources. The report covers federal lands administered by the Departments of Agriculture, Defense, Energy and Interior, as well as the Tennessee Valley Authority. It also highlights substantial, but less thoroughly studied, coal resources in Alaska, where USGS estimates at least 140 billion short tons and identifies the potential for considerably more. The assessment follows a 2025 executive order directing Interior to evaluate coal resources beneath federal lands and reflects the Department’s broader effort to facilitate domestic energy development. --- Jason Wandling MSHA Announces Overhaul of Alternative Case Resolution Procedures to Streamline Enforcement Actions, Maintain Consistency “Conference Litigation Representatives and Special Investigators will no longer report to District Managers.” Why this is important: The Mine Safety and Health Administration (MSHA) has established a new Conference Litigation and Investigative Resources (CLIR) group to address operator concerns over enforcement actions before cases go into formal litigation. The new system could result in less litigation through the early settlement of enforcement disputes while potentially strengthening enforcement at the mine site level. The new system will handle conference requests for citations and orders served on mine operators and special investigation (110c) charges against agents of the operator. However, the new system will not address citations and orders for accidents, fatalities or complex legal issues. Previously, operators would request 10-day conferences and the conferences were then handled at the district level by conference officers who reported to the same district manager and who likely reviewed, and in many cases, recommended or approved the enforcement actions. Under the new system, operators must still request a conference in writing within 10 days of the citation or order being issued and explain why they believe each citation or order should be reviewed and what needs to be changed. Conference Litigation and Investigative Resources representatives (CLIRs) will then have the authority to grant conferences with operators and review the facts of each case. They would also get the company's position on what should be changed and why. CLIRs can then modify citations if the facts warrant changes. Approval of any settlement will not be made by the District Manager. The CLIR administration, now located in Beckley, West Virginia, will make final decisions on any changes to the citations or orders. The remaining citations or orders with any modifications are then sent to the Office of Assessments for processing and calculation of a penalty. Mine operators continue to have a right to request a hearing before an Administrative Law Judge of the Federal Mine Safety Health and Review Commission within 30 days of receiving the assessment form. The new system has the potential to reduce case litigation before the Federal Mine Safety and Health Review Commission through the early settlement of cases without having to litigate before the Commission. --- Mark E. Heath Virginia to Cut Rooftop Solar Costs with Nation-First Bulk-Buy Program “Virginia is the first to try a statewide campaign as utility bills rise and data centers stress the grid.” Why this is important: Virginia is implementing a program to buy solar panels in bulk to reduce the cost of installing rooftop solar. The “Switch Together” program allows homeowners and installers to buy in bulk and, with larger purchases, obtain solar panels at a reduced cost. Solar United Neighbors runs the Virginia state program and for years has pooled purchases at the local level. By expanding the program statewide, they expect to lower solar costs at a time when utility rates are rising with increased demand and data center construction. They believe the increase in solar will reduce strain on the electrical grid and save homeowners on their electric bills. Since the program started in July, 4,300 homeowners have requested information and 120 have signed contracts. When the promotion ends on October 15, the group expects about 5,000 inquiries and 500 contracts for solar panel installation will be signed. The group believes that could total 4 MWs of electric power from the new solar panels, which could save individual homeowners about $2,200 per year. The effort is designed to reduce solar costs after the Trump administration led efforts to eliminate solar tax credits. --- Mark E. Heath East Coast States are Losing a Key Power Source as Offshore Wind Projects Stall, Shrink, or Vanish “As of mid-August, roughly $4 billion had been set aside for those buyouts, eliminating about 21 gigawatts of potential wind capacity — enough to power more than 15 million typical U.S. households, according to Grist.” Why this is important: The Trump administration is spending in excess of $4 billion to buy out previously granted and paid-for leases for offshore wind farms. The leases were authorized by the previous federal administration under President Biden and operators purchased the leases and began construction. Now the administration is using tax dollars to buy out the leases to prevent offshore wind from being developed. The leases that have been bought out would have produced 21 GWs of electricity, enough to power 15 million homes. In addition to buying out leases, the Trump administration has revoked permits, issued stop work orders, and ordered offshore wind farms to undergo Pentagon review before construction could begin. While the tactics have resulted in the cancellation of a number of offshore wind farms, others have gone into operation. It is also likely the same tactics used to stop offshore wind could be used by a new administration to stop the fossil fuel plant development now being pushed by the Trump administration. --- Mark E. title: Newcastle v Hull City: Key stats and talking points - Yahoo Sports
content: Newcastle United seek a first home league win of the season as they face high-flying Hull City, the only team to play at St James' Park more than once in the Premier League and never lose (W2, D1). Throughout Newcastle's unbeaten five-match start to the season, it was evident that this vibrant young team is, as is the nature of any rebuild, a work in progress. Monday night's bruising 4-1 defeat by Leeds merely brought the shortcomings into sharper focus. Matthias Jaissle's side had been defying some underlying metrics in the opening three league games, which made their positive start to the season look unsustainable. "We need to expect ups and downs," Jaissle has admitted. Putting aside the fact Newcastle were uncharacteristically outfought by Leeds, they have issues to address at both ends of the pitch – some predating the £265m-plus squad overhaul this summer. Newcastle have conceded 39 goals in 23 Premier League games this calendar year – only Crystal Palace and Chelsea have a worse record – and kept just two clean sheets in the last 20 of those. This season, the mid-table Magpies have faced the most shots in the division, while only three teams should have conceded more goals based on the quality of chances against them. In attack, Newcastle have had the joint-second fewest shots but scored seven times from an expected goals tally of 3.9. While the use of xG is divisive among football supporters, it does suggest an over-performance in front of goal that will be hard for Newcastle to sustain. Fourth-placed Hull City are looking to become the first promoted Premier League side to avoid defeat in their opening five games since Portsmouth in 2003-04. Their impressive adaptation to the Premier League has come about while doubling down on last season's style of play. Hull have averaged just 29.3% possession this season but pressed their opponents aggressively and more often than any other side to win the ball and start swift counter attacks. Tellingly, the core of the team which earned promotion are still entrusted with implementing this approach – despite the club signing 18 players this summer. Seven or more of the starting XI in each of Hull's Premier League games so far were at the club last season, aiding the continuity of tactics and a feeling of togetherness. Eight of the 11 Hull players who have spent the most time on the pitch to date were part of the promotion-winning squad. Overall, players who were at the club last season account for 67% of minutes played by the Tigers in the Premier League.

title: Everton v Ipswich: Key stats and talking points - Yahoo Sports
content: Everton aim to continue their unbeaten start against an Ipswich side bidding for back-to-back away wins. BBC Sport examines some of the key themes going into their meeting at Hill Dickinson Stadium on Saturday. The win over Wolves in the Carabao Cup on Wednesday provided the dual positives of extending Everton's unbeaten start to the season and allowing fringe players to come to the fore. Second-half substitute Charly Alcaraz scored the winner after 80 minutes – his first goal for the club in 13 months – on his longest outing of the season so far. Winger Tyler Dibling also impressed on what was only his eighth start since swapping Southampton for Merseyside in a £35m move a year ago, assisting the winning goal, while Brennan Johnson, usually utilised out wide, was effective as a central striker after replacing Thierno Barry. The flexibility and impact of squad members is a welcome boon for manager David Moyes given he was limited to selecting from just 15 fit senior outfield players for the cup tie. Christian Norgaard, Harrison Armstrong and Merlin Rohl are injured, and while Armstrong could return this weekend, Everton's arduous end to the summer transfer window is already being exacerbated by fitness issues. The EFL Cup victory means that Everton prepare to face Ipswich Town having started their campaign by going undefeated in six games in for the first time since 2020-21, while it is only the second time in either Moyes reign that the Blue have gone unbeaten in their opening four Premier League matches. While the midweek fixture was decided by players still earning their manager's trust, Everton's most recent league outing was influenced by somebody already assured of Moyes's good graces. James Garner's all-action performance in the goalless draw at Tottenham was pivotal in earning a hard-earned point and a return to his superlative form of last season following groin surgery before this campaign. Garner's physicality, creativity and versatility are all likely to be crucial assets if the Toffees are to push back towards the European places this season, but also in matches against unpredictable opposition. Ipswich have impressed in beating Sunderland and Crystal Palace already this season, while they were competitive during the early stages of the defeat at Manchester United. The Tractor Boys have earned six points after four matches, having taken 16 matches to do so during their previous Premier League campaign in 2024-25. However, they are only the third team in the competition's history to earn six points at this stage while conceding as many as 10 goals. The juxtaposition of Ipswich's points and goals-against tallies point to a side playing more open football than in their tactical approach to the top flight two years ago. A key part of that increased ambition has been the threat posed by summer signing Julio Enciso. The 22-year-old tops most of Ipswich's attacking metrics, including touches in the opposition box (14), shots (14) and dribbles (20), while he has also drawn more fouls resulting in a card for an opponent than any other Premier League player this season. Enciso also has form for troubling Everton having scored to help earn a 2-2 draw at Goodison Park in May 2025 while on loan from Brighton, on Ipswich's most recent trip to the blue half of Merseyside. The hero last time out, however, was Zian Flemming, another summer signing scoring his first goal for the club in the 90th minute to seal a 3-2 win at Selhurst Park. Flemming's involvement will not be lost on Moyes given Everton were reportedly interested on deadline day, nor Ipswich's summer outlay of £185m – a sharp contrast to Everton's trading profit of £25.4m. Ipswich boss Gary O'Neil will hope the club's recruitment drive will prove decisive as he hunts a first Premier League victory as a manager against Moyes, having lost all four meetings so far. His Everton counterpart can only hope his whole squad continues to contribute across the course of this season.

title: Brighton v Arsenal: Key stats and talking points - Yahoo Sports
content: BBC Sport examines some of the key themes before Saturday's match between Brighton and Arsenal (15:00 BST), with the Gunners looking to make it five league wins from five before the international break. Brighton's 5-0 victory at Coventry City equalled their biggest Premier League away win and took their tally to 13 goals from their opening four matches, a club record at this stage of a top-flight season. The result also made them the league's top scorers after four matchrounds. That is no fluke, with the Seagulls the only team to have accumulated an expected goals total of 10 or more. But they have also made the most of their chances, scoring almost three goals more than Opta's xG model would predict, helped by long-range strikes from Lewis Dunk and Yasin Ayari last weekend. Brighton demonstrated their firepower again in midweek, with 19-year-old Greek striker Charalampos Kostoulas scoring for the second successive game as they came from 2-0 down to win 3-2 at Manchester United in the Carabao Cup. Fabian Hurzeler's free-scoring side will, however, face a tougher test against the league's strongest defensive unit. Brighton have not beaten Arsenal at home for six years and lost all three league and cup meetings between the sides last season. After a scare at Sunderland, where David Raya's penalty save proved decisive, Arsenal made it seven wins from seven this season by beating Ipswich Town in the EFL Cup on Tuesday. Max Dowman scored twice at Portman Road, becoming only the second 16-year-old, after Wayne Rooney, to net a double for a Premier League side. But Dowman, who has yet to feature in the top flight this season, may have to bide his time for further opportunities given his team's impressive form. The Gunners are seeking a 10th consecutive league victory, a feat they last achieved in 2002. Another win on Saturday would leave them four short of the club record, set in 1998. Arsenal have conceded just twice in their previous nine league games and have barely missed a beat this term, despite the absence of key centre-back William Saliba. They have conceded only once in the league in 2026-27, while their totals for shots faced, shots on target faced and expected goals against are all the lowest in the division.

title: Sutton's predictions: Tottenham v Aston Villa - Yahoo Sports
content: Tottenham boss Roberto de Zerbi has this reputation of being a great coach. We saw what a good job he did at Brighton, but we haven't seen any improvement from Spurs yet, despite the big money they have spent. He is surely going to come under pressure soon, if their poor results continue. They are not the only ones to revamp their squad but, if you listen to De Zerbi, after about five years they might come good. He keeps saying they need time, but he's had long enough for their results to be much better already. Other clubs, like Hull City and Ipswich Town, have brought plenty of players in and are doing well enough - so why aren't Spurs? I think De Zerbi has to come under scrutiny, but it is different with Unai Emery at Aston Villa. They are also without a league win, but they look more likely to score goals, as they showed against Coventry City in the Carabao Cup on Wednesday. I'm expecting them to improve the same way they did after not winning any of their first five games last season, and I can see them edging this. Do I give Spurs their first league goal of the season? Yes, but only one. They are due a deflection or Villa will score an own goal.

title: V for Vendetta Returning to Theaters in November, Thanks to Fathom - Consequence of Sound
content: Log in to track artists, discover shows, and stay in the loop. The 2006 movie, starring Natalie Portman and Hugo Weaving, will be back this November (the 5th, of course) Remember, remember, the fifth of November — because that’s when the 2006 dystopian drama V for Vendetta will be returning to theaters in celebration of its 20th anniversary. Thanks to Fathom, tickets are now officially on sale for director James McTeigue’s adaptation of Alan Miller and David Lloyd’s seminal graphic novel, written for the screen by the Wachowskis. title: Premier League action, Celtic v Rangers, T20 cricket and NFL – follow with us - The Guardian
content: Here’s how to follow along with our coverage – the finest writing and up-to-the-minute reports Michael Butler rises early to barge open the door to Saturday’s football activity. He will be offering breaking news and updates from around the grounds in the buildup to five Premier League games, starting with the lunchtime meeting of the 17th and 19th clubs in the table, big names down on their uppers: Tottenham and Aston Villa, respectively. He won’t be forgetting the Championship, which braces for the renewal of two bitter feuds when the leaders, West Ham, travel to the Den on Saturday to face their London rivals Millwall for the first time in 14 years. Join the conversation by emailing your thoughts and queries to matchday.live@theguardian.com After a summer spend in excess of £300m, things were supposed to be different this season ⁠after successive 17th-placed finishes. Instead, after four games, that is exactly where Tottenham find themselves again after no ​wins – and not a single goal – in their opening ​four games. Roberto De Zerbi remained confident after Tuesday’s League Cup ​loss at Liverpool that his side would “click” soon and the early kick-off at home to an Aston Villa side with ​only one point so far would ‌be an opportune moment for ​that to happen – for both teams. Daniel Gallan helms the liveblog with Paul MacInnes our match reporter. James Wallace has over-by-over coverage of the third T20 after Harry Brook’s side overpowered Sri Lanka for the second time in three days, a six-wicket win in Cardiff being achieved with 7.5 overs to spare on Thursday. It gave England an insurmountable 2-0 lead in the three-match series, which has come on the back of beating India 4-0 earlier in the summer. In fact, England have won 22 of their past 25 matches in the short format of the game. Brook bludgeoned 114 not out from 49 balls in the opening win at Southampton, and this time Tom Banton got England over the line with an unbeaten 52 off 24 deliveries. Banton’s pivotal innings came after Jos Buttler became the first player to reach 15,000 runs in T20 cricket. Tanya Aldred will report from Old Trafford. Scott Murray is at the controls with regular updates from the three Premier League mid-afternoon kick-offs. Front and centre will be the pacesetters and champions, Arsenal. They head to the south coast amid an ominous start to their Premier League defence after taking four victories from four but face the trickiest of trips, away to Brighton, whose tally of 13 goals from four games is the highest in the division. Monday’s 4-1 thrashing at Leeds was certainly a wake-up call for Matthias Jaissle. Defeat ended Newcastle’s unbeaten start this season and an injury-hit squad now face high-flying Hull at St James’ Park. Sergej Jakirovic’s side are fourth in the table with two wins and two draws, holding Chelsea 2-2 in their last outing. Renée Slegers’ Gunners stride out at the Emirates Stadium unbeaten, although they were frustrated in a scoreless draw with promoted Crystal Palace last weekend. Eva Olid’s Manchester United tenure has begun with defeats in both their opening games, and they have conceded seven goals, more than any other WSL team so far. Olid is expecting a response from their 5-0 trashing by Chelsea last weekend. “My main message is about being themselves,” she said. “I am not sure they are showing in the first two matches who they are and what they can do. For me it is so important that they show that to perform. We had a day to reflect and analyse the game, to see what we can do better and we know what we have to do.” Will Magee has minute-by-minute coverage, and Tom Garry reports. Sunday brings four Premier League matches plus an Old Firm derby and a spicy clash at Molineux as Wolves host old foes West Brom. Emillia Hawkins is on hand bright and early with all the breaking news at the helm of our essential football live blog. Join the conversation by emailing your thoughts and queries to matchday.live@theguardian.com Celtic have a 100% league record but are in something of a tailspin, having been thumped 3-0 in the League Cup by their Glasgow rivals at Ibrox on Sunday and then beaten 3-1 by Ferencvaros at Parkhead in the Europa League on Thursday. So it is less than an optimal moment to be going up against Rangers, who will be striving to make it six wins in succession across all competitions when they visit Celtic Park. Martin O’Neill certainly understands his side are a world away from last season’s uplift, calling their latest loss “a huge frustration” and “psychologically damning”. He admitted: “It’s not the start we wanted. Really need to concentrate now on Sunday [against Rangers] … Sunday’s a big game.” John Brewin helms the blog with Jonathan Liew reporting. Liverpool remain unbeaten under their new head coach, Andoni Iraola, in all competitions but managing three draws from four Premier League games has stifled any early-season momentum. Iraola will be back in familiar surroundings as his side travel to Bournemouth, the south coast club the Spaniard consistently had punching above their weight. Bournemouth are yet ‌to win in the league under Iraola’s replacement, Marco Rose, but three draws and a rather unlucky loss at Manchester City are scant return for some eye-catching football under the German. Daniel Harris has the live blog, with Ben Fisher reporting. One month into the Premier League season, excuses about bedding-in processes and newly assembled squads needing time to gel are wearing thin and for Manchester United there is ⁠an acute sense of urgency as the international break looms. After so much pre-season optimism, the spotlight has turned on the ⁠manager, Michael Carrick. Only one ​win in four league games – at home to promoted Ipswich – has been compounded by Wednesday’s League Cup exit at home to Brighton, having led 2-0. Another setback at Craven Cottage against a ⁠Fulham side without a league win would increase the pressure on Carrick and deepen the sense that United’s season is in danger of drifting before it has properly begun. United will be buoyed by the fact they ‌have not lost at Fulham since 2009, but while the London club have made a slow start under Álvaro Arbeloa, a draw at Liverpool last week and a League Cup win at West Ham in midweek offered glimpses of better things to come. Taha Hashim brings the noise in the live blog, with David Hytner and Jacob Steinberg our reporting team at Craven Cottage. Graham Searles is back for the best of week two’s action. He will be concentrating on Vikings v Bears and Steelers v Patriots from the eight 6pm fixtures. Minnesota opened their season with a comeback win over Green Bay, rallying from a 12-point deficit late in the third quarter to overwhelm the Packers. The Vikings’ defense will bid to shut down Caleb Williams in a battle of unbeaten teams after the Chicago quarterback inspired a record-breaking start to the season. Williams threw two touchdowns and ran for two more as the Bears pounded the Carolina Panthers 59-37 last weekend in the highest-scoring opener in NFL history. Pittsburgh, meanwhile, are coming off the successful debut of their new coach, Mike McCarthy, after the departure of Mike Tomlin, and a vintage effort from their 42-year-old quarterback Aaron Rodgers in their opening win over Atlanta. The Patriots will be entering their second home opener under Mike Vrabel, the architect of New England’s renaissance in the post-Tom Brady era, and with a third-year quarterback in Drake Maye whose post-Super Bowl run honeymoon appears to be over after one of the worst performances of his young career in last week’s 13-10 loss to Seattle.

title: State of Florida v. Michael Alan Smith - 7th Judicial Circuit State Attorney's Office
content: Smith Convicted of Aggravated Assault on Orange City Police Officer DELAND – After a full-day trial, a Volusia County jury found defendant Michael Smith guilty as charged of Aggravated Assault on Law Enforcement Officer (Deadly Weapon), Resisting an Officer with Violence and Display of a Weapon during Commission of a Felony. Immediately following the verdict, the jury qualified the defendant as a Habitual Felony Offender based on his violent criminal history. In 1994, he was convicted of Second-Degree Murder and Aggravated Battery with a Deadly Weapon in Marion County and was sentenced to 27 years in prison. On Jan. 27, 2026, Smith was standing on a sidewalk near a busy Orange City shopping complex with a stab wound to the neck. An Orange City Police Officer responded to the location to assist him. The officer immediately noticed Smith had a knife in his hand and repeatedly commanded him to drop it. Instead of complying, the defendant made aggressive movements toward the officer with the knife. Over the next five minutes, Smith walked and ran away from the officer, ignoring continued commands to stop and drop the knife. The officer attempted to subdue him with a Taser, but it didn’t work because his jacket blocked the probes. As Smith began entering a bank, the officer shot him in the lower back. Even with the gunshot wound, the defendant continued into the bank and still refused to drop his knife. Other officers arrived shortly after and took him into custody. Despite his extremely reckless behavior, no employees or customers in the bank were injured. Smith was taken to the hospital, where he recovered from his injuries. “This case is an example of what your law enforcement officers deal with on a daily basis,” State Attorney R.J. Larizza said about the case. “They risk their lives so you can be safe. Please let them know you appreciate their efforts on your behalf.” The case was investigated by the Orange City Police Department with assistance from the Volusia Sheriff’s Office. Assistant State Attorney Nick Kramperth successfully tried the case for the State of Florida. The Honorable Karen Foxman heard the case and is set to impose sentence on Oct. 21, 2026. Smith faces up to 30 years in prison for the convictions. Haley Harrison | Public Information Officer | Office of State Attorney R.J. title: ITIA v Romeo Arcuschin - Sport Resolutions
content: A decision in the case of International Tennis Integrity Agency (ITIA) against Romeo Arcuschin (the Player) has been issued by the Independent Panel. On 15 December 2025, while competing at the ITF World Tennis Tour M15 event in Lima, Peru, an In-Competition urine Sample was collected from Mr Arcuschin, a then 18-year-old Argentinean International-Level tennis player. On 16 February 2026, the ITIA notified the Player of the presence of Stanozolol metabolites and Clomifene detected in his Sample. Stanozolol is a non-Specified substance, listed in the category of Anabolic Agents (Section S1.1. of the 2025 World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA) Prohibited List). Clomifene is a Specified substance, listed in the category of Hormone and Metabolic Modulators (Section S4.2. of the 2025 WADA Prohibited List). A mandatory Provisional Suspension was imposed with immediate effect. On 7 March 2026, the Player submitted a written response stating that he admitted the Anti-Doping Rule Violations (ADRVs) and was contesting the Consequences, as they are set out in the Tennis Anti-Doping Programme (TADP). The Player also provided an explanation of how the Prohibited Substances came to be in his body. On 13 March 2026, the ITIA formally charged the Player with four (4) ADRVs under TADP 2026 Articles 2.1 and/or 2.2, based on the presence of Stanozolol and Clomifene found in his Sample. On 11 August 2026, a hearing took place before the Independent Tribunal, which comprised David Casement KC (Chair), Dr Chinyere Ezewuzie, and Dr Tanja Haug, who were appointed from the Independent Panel to hear this matter. Whilst not disputing that the Prohibited Substances had been found in his Sample, Mr Arcuschin sought to reduce the period of Ineligibility of four (4) years, set out in TADP Article 10.2.1, to a minimum of one (1) year, by establishing that his conduct had not been intentional and that he bore No Significant Fault or Negligence in committing the ADRVs. The Player maintained, and it was accepted by the ITIA, that, on 27 February 2025, whilst competing, he fell on his left side. The fall caused the Player’s left shoulder to dislocate. While medical staff treated the Player, he suffered a second dislocation. After a period of immobilisation and treatment, the Player continued to suffer recurrent yet irregular dislocations of his left shoulder. On 1 May 2025, the Player underwent surgery, which caused a decrease in strength of about 15% in the affected shoulder. On 7 August 2025, the Player consulted another doctor, who had come recommended to him. It was then that the Player was prescribed a 30-day-course of compounded medications, which consisted of Stanozolol and Clomifene, to treat the muscle atrophy in his shoulder and arm. Both the Player and the doctor confirmed to the Independent Tribunal that, when the prescription was issued to the Player, neither the medication nor the potential side effects were explained by the doctor. The prescription was also illegible. The Player simply took the prescription to a pharmacy, where he received the medication in two bottles, without labels or instructions. The Player maintained that, as he had not received any anti-doping education, he was completely unaware of what he was about to ingest or of the potential risk he was undertaking. The ITIA sought to discern when, during the period he was treating the Player, the doctor became aware that the Player was a professional athlete and was therefore subject to anti-doping rules. The ITIA insisted that the Player knew the prescription contained Prohibited Substances and that the reason he had made an appointment with the doctor, without informing his support or medical teams, and had not undertaken any research into the doctor, was not because of unawareness from a lack of anti-doping education. Rather, it was because the Player knew of the doctor’s prominent practice treating bodybuilders. Further, the doctor confirmed that he never informed the Player that the prescription contained Prohibited Substances and that, even if the Player had asked, he would not have disclosed what was contained in the compound medications. In carefully considering the parties’ submissions, the Tribunal recognised the great imbalance in status between the doctor and the Player. Despite acknowledging the doctor’s extensive experience as a medical practitioner, particularly in sports medicine, the Tribunal also took into account that the doctor gave no information to the Player about the substances he was prescribing, while expressly and implicitly reassuring the Player that there was nothing to be concerned about. Given the serious Consequences any athlete who ingests Prohibited Substances might face, the Tribunal noted that the doctor ought to have asked the Player whether he was playing professionally and whether he was subject to anti-doping rules. The Tribunal also accounted for the Player’s age and the particular circumstances he was facing at the time and concluded that his mind was far from focused on anti-doping regulations, of which he had little knowledge to begin with. Although the Player had completed two multiple-choice tests, in which a select number of questions related to anti-doping, this did not, in the view of the Tribunal, constitute education. In any event, the fact that the Player struggled to correctly answer the anti-doping questions on the multiple-choice tests evidenced his lack of knowledge and his need for education. Consequently, the Tribunal accepted that the Player placed his absolute trust in a senior doctor and that, given the disparity in age, experience, and authority, together with his own youth and inexperience, the Player did not question the medications he was given. The Tribunal therefore concluded that the Player proved, on the balance of probabilities, that his conduct leading to the ingestion of Stanozolol was not intentional. In respect of Clomifene, the Tribunal found that, for the same reasons, the ITIA had not discharged its burden of proof to show that the Player’s conduct had been intentional. In assessing Mr Arcuschin’s degree of Fault and determining the appropriate sanction to be imposed, the Tribunal remained mindful of TADP 2026 Articles 2.1.1 and 2.2.1, which confirm that the Player is responsible for everything that enters his body, and that it is his responsibility to comply with the anti-doping rules. When taken into account against the Player’s unquestioning and total reliance upon the doctor’s advice, advice that was substantially lacking in important information, the Tribunal determined that Fault could not be laid entirely on the Player. The Tribunal therefore imposed a twenty (20)-month-long period of Ineligibility. The period of Ineligibility commenced on 28 August 2026, the date of the decision, with time served on Provisional Suspension being credited. Further, Mr Arcuschin’s results obtained at the ITF World Tennis Tour M15 event, and all subsequent events achieved prior to his Provisional Suspension, are Disqualified with all resulting Consequences, including forfeiture of all medals, titles, ranking points, and Prize Money, pursuant to TADP Articles 9.1, 10.1, and 10.10. content: A new report suggests the next CR-V will begin production in early 2027. Honda took the axe to its whole EV operation earlier this year, leaving it with a few holes in its lineup. Now, it could be fast-tracking the development and launch of next-generation hybrid vehicles, starting with the CR-V. As reported by Nikkei, Honda is moving up the launch and production of its next-gen CR-V to February 2027. The current model isn’t especially old, considering it went on sale in late 2022 as a 2023 model year vehicle. That said, it’s Honda’s most popular vehicle here in the U.S., so keeping it competitive with other hybrid compact SUVs like the Toyota RAV4 (now hybrid-only) is vital. Nikkei reports that the CR-V that launches next year will be a full redesign of the current model. It’s set to be fitted with Honda’s next-generation hybrid technology, which we suspect will be an evolution of the company’s two-motor hybrid system it’s used for years. The report doesn’t specify whether or not this CR-V will be hybrid-only or continue to offer a purely gas-powered variant, but we wouldn’t be surprised to see Honda follow in Toyota’s footsteps and go all-in on its excellent hybrid powertrain. In addition to this Honda news, the report says Acura will launch a new hybrid vehicle based on this next-gen CR-V. The RDX has long been Acura’s CR-V-like SUV offering in terms of size and use case. However, Acura said in January that the next RDX was “planned for market introduction in the next couple of years,” suggesting it will launch much later than this next-gen CR-V. We already knew Honda was developing a three-row hybrid SUV based on previous reports, but this latest report from Nikkei further confirms the presence of such a vehicle. The plan would be for that model to launch in 2029. Instead of the four-cylinder two-motor hybrid powertrain, a V-6-based two-motor hybrid system is reportedly being developed that would power this large hybrid vehicle. Road & Track reached out to Honda about this report and received the following statement in response. “This was not announced by Honda. While we cannot comment on specific future product plans, as outlined in our 2026 Business Update, Honda remains on track to introduce next-generation HEV models beginning in 2027, featuring an all-new hybrid system and platform.” We may earn commission from links on this page, but we only recommend products we back.

title: 20 Years Later, the Greatest Dystopian Sci-Fi Movie Ever Made Officially Returns to Theaters - Collider
content: Remember, remember, the fifth of November. Some movies can become less relevant as times change, and politics shift, but some of them remain eerily prescient and, dare we say, timeless. An anonymous Robin Hood, or terrorist, depending on your point of view. Fighting with authority and government, battling surveillance, propaganda, fear, and the erosion of individual freedom — these issues haven't exactly vanished, and that explains why one of the 2000s’ most distinctive dystopian movies refuses to disappear. Based on the graphic novel by Alan Moore and David Lloyd, and set against the futuristic landscape of totalitarian Britain, V For Vendetta tells the story of a mild-mannered young woman named Evey who is rescued from a life-and-death situation by a masked man known only as ‘V.’ Incomparably charismatic and ferociously skilled in the art of combat and deception, V ignites a revolution when he urges his fellow citizens to rise up against tyranny and oppression. As Evey uncovers the truth about V’s mysterious background, she also discovers the truth about herself, and emerges as his unlikely ally in the culmination of his plan to bring freedom and justice back to a society fraught with cruelty and corruption. Twenty years after its original release, V for Vendetta is officially returning to theaters for two nights only on November 1 and November 5, courtesy of Fathom Entertainment, Warner Bros., and DC Vertigo. Tickets are now on sale for the anniversary event, which will present James McTeigue’s (Ninja Assassin) dystopian thriller on the big screen alongside an exclusive new featurette featuring the director. The cast is led by Natalie Portman (Black Swan) as Evey Hammond and Hugo Weaving (The Matrix) as V, alongside Stephen Rea (The Crying Game) as Eric Finch, Stephen Fry (Gosford Park) as Gordon Deitrich, John Hurt (Alien) as Adam Sutler, Rupert Graves (Sherlock) as Dominic Stone, Roger Allam (Endeavour) as Lewis Prothero, and Tim Pigott-Smith (Quantum of Solace) as Peter Creedy. Your answers point to the world your instincts were built for. This is the universe your temperament, your survival instincts, and your particular brand of stubbornness were made for. You took the red pill a long time ago — probably before anyone offered it to you. You're a systems thinker who can't help but notice the seams in things. The wasteland doesn't reward the clever or the well-connected — it rewards those who are hard to kill and harder to break. That's you. You'd survive here because you know how to exist in moral grey areas without losing yourself completely. Arrakis is the most hostile environment in the known universe — and you are precisely the kind of person it rewards. The galaxy far, far away is vast, loud, and in a constant state of violent political upheaval — and you wouldn't have it any other way. McTeigue spoke at length with Collider earlier this year about why the movie’s politics have continued resonating long after its original release. He feels the issues explored in the movie are "timeless" because they aren't unique to any particular time period, but are issues every generation will deal with. “I feel like V has become timeless because it didn’t try to lean too much into the politics of the day. It tried to give you this overview of political systems and people that exist in them, and individual freedoms that always exist within those political systems, but wrapped up in an anti-superhero movie. I don’t think I would have changed anything just because the parallels are there, and they’ll be there in 40 years, and they’ll be there in 60 years.” Perhaps the movie’s most extraordinary legacy isn’t actually on screen. The stylized Guy Fawkes mask worn by V escaped the confines of the movie and became an internationally recognizable symbol of protest, subsequently appearing during demonstrations around the world. McTeigue told Collider that watching an element created for the movie take on an entirely separate cultural meaning was something he could never have predicted: “The mask lived on, and people really understood what the mask represented, which was there was more power in a group of people, and the mask let people protest in a way they couldn’t have before. So, I think the film resonated that way. It sort of spread its tentacles out into society, and so now, just about everyone in the world knows what a Guy Fawkes mask is, right? It’s an amazing thing for your film to slip into the culture like that. It’s a one-in-a-million shot sometimes.” V for Vendetta returns to theaters for its 20th anniversary on November 1 and November 5, 2026. We want to hear from you.
